Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, procurement-friendly response; Sergio and Neha are cc'd for technical and compliance detail. We're happy to produce an attestation and supporting manifests once you confirm the tenant ID we should reference.

Summary (hosted API):

1) What we consider customer data
- Request payloads: any content in the POST body to the text/chat/embedding endpoints.
- Response tokens: generated outputs returned to the customer.
- Audit & operational logs: processing traces, per-request latency and error logs which may include metadata (tenant ID, request id, timestamps).
- KV/prefix cache: transient cached key/value pairs or prefix tokens used only to speed inference. These are ephemeral and scoped to the tenant.
- Backups & snapshots: encrypted storage snapshots created for disaster recovery of internal service state (not model weights). May contain tenant data depending on timing.

2) Retention windows (default hosted plan)
- Request payloads & response tokens: retained for up to 30 days for routing, caching, and abuse detection.
- Operational logs (searchable): retained 90 days by default; aggregated metrics retained 24 months.
- KV/prefix cache: kept in-memory or on local ephemeral SSD; entries are evicted based on LRU and never intentionally persisted beyond 48 hours.
- Backups/snapshots (DR): rolling backups retained for up to 30 days; snapshots are immutable for 7 days before rotation.

3) Deletion / customer handback process
- Immediate: Upon a tenant deletion/erasure request via the console or API (customer-data-delete), we queue a tenant-scoped erasure job that removes active request payloads, responses, and tenant metadata from primary stores within 72 hours.
- Cache eviction: KV/prefix cache entries are invalidated immediately and will be evicted from memory within 48 hours.
- Backups & snapshots: We initiate a background purge of tenant data in backups. Due to backup immutability, the final scrub completes within 30 days; we mark records as inaccessible for production from the time of request (no reads) and schedule physical removal from backups per the 30-day window.
- Attestation: We can provide a signed erasure attestation with the timestamped job id and affected manifests after the purge completes.

4) Evidence & auditability
- Audit logs (read-only) show the deletion job creation, worker progression, and finalization. We can export a manifest (list of affected object ids) and a signed S3 manifest for your review.
- SOC2 control mappings and our deletion runbook are available; we can produce a tailored attestation for procurement.

Attachments included: security-supplement.pdf (summary of controls), srh-data-handback-playbook.docx (provisional playbook referencing SRH tenant ID once provided).

If you want stricter windows (e.g., 7-day primary retention, 14-day backup scrub), we can discuss an enterprise contract variation.

Best,

Hi Aisha — quick technical clarifications to Marissa's note: please treat this as the implementation detail for your security team.

- Primary stores: request/response bodies are stored in an encrypted object store (AES-256) with per-tenant prefixes. When the erasure job runs, we delete objects under that prefix and write a tombstone entry to our internal index. Tombstones are themselves short-lived and are removed after the next index compaction (typically 7 days) to avoid accidental rehydration.

- Backups: our nightly backups are incremental; tenants may appear in multiple increments. The deletion pipeline rewrites the incremental index to exclude the tenant's objects; since old increments are immutable, we mark them for overwrite and the data becomes inaccessible immediately, but the physical blocks are reclaimed during our 30-day backup retention cycle.

- KV/Inference cache: KV cache is stored on local NVMe on the inference nodes, not in durable object storage. The eviction timeline is governed by TTL or LRU; on erasure we push an invalidation event and proactive eviction which typically clears relevant blocks within 48 hours.

- Evidence: we'll provide a signed S3 manifest AND an internal deletion_run_{ticket}.log containing worker-level timestamps. If you need a readout in a specific format (CSV/JSON), say the word and we'll deliver.

Operational note: deletion jobs are auditable and create a support ticket automatically; the ticket id will be included in the attestation. For compliance reviews we can schedule a short runbook walkthrough with your SecOps team.

— Sergio Alvarez
